lines.text: Going down took him twelve minutes.
Coming back up took nearly fifteen hours.
Dahab, Egypt, 2014. Ahmed Gabr drops into the Red Sea.
No submarine. Just scuba tanks and a rope.
One hundred metres. Two hundred. Three hundred.
Tags on the rope will prove the depth.
Deeper than the Eiffel Tower is tall.
A new world record. The old mark had stood since 2005.
Now the hard part: getting back.
Rise too fast, and gas in his body forms bubbles. The bends.
So he climbs slowly, stop after stop, through dozens of gas tanks.
Nearly fifteen hours after he left, he breaks the surface.
Six years later, anonymous critics claimed the evidence didn't add up.
Its conclusion: he did reach three hundred and thirty-two metres.
Twelve minutes to set it. Nearly fifteen hours to survive it.
